budget_matched_records.confound_note: In-File vs RepoCoder varies both the presence of retrieval and its content (no cross-file budget at all vs a fixed K=10 retrieval budget); the more controlled contrast (Iter-1/Iter-2 vs Oracle) holds K and window sizes constant while varying only query quality (self-predicted vs ground-truth continuation).

RepoBench-R's central comparison varies only the retrieval method (lexical Jaccard/Edit-Sim vs. semantic CodeBERT/UniXcoder embeddings) over the same candidate snippets and prompt structure; RepoBench-C/P separately vary completion model and the 2k-vs-8k budget together, so those are not budget-matched representation ablations.
Primary comparison (§4.1) varies only presence/absence of monitor-guided logit masking; prompting strategy, decoding parameters, and token budgets are held constant, isolating the mechanism's effect.

Retriever/representation varied (BM25 lexical vs UniXCoder/ada dense embeddings) at matched top-5 snippets / 512-token budget in the retrieval-method comparison; the separate with-vs-without-context comparison additionally varies budget (0 vs 512 tokens).

Table 1's core comparison (analogy-only vs. rationale-only vs. dual context) holds the 4096-token truncation budget fixed and varies only which context type(s) the RTG algorithm ranks/merges; Figure 3 separately varies the budget itself (512-4096 tokens) to show dual context's efficiency, which is a distinct, budget-varying analysis.

Table 5 ablation (with/without abstract context, with/without snippet context) varies representation composition only, holding the N=4,096-token prompt budget and retrieval method (Jaccard) fixed — a budget-matched representation ablation; Table 2/4 main results vary model, fine-tuning, and benchmark simultaneously, not budget-matched.

Both representation (CCG control/data-dependence graph vs RepoCoder's iterative regeneration-retrieval) and mechanism vary simultaneously; token counts differ between methods rather than being held constant.

Six independent benchmark tasks each vary both the underlying model and the context-assembly strategy (raw window vs BM25/embedding retrieval vs full-repo file lists) simultaneously; this is a multi-task benchmark suite of separate baselines, not one controlled ablation.

Headline comparison (Random-All baseline vs HCP) varies both representation (flat concatenation vs hierarchical dependency-graph+embedding pruning) and token budget (~50k vs ~8k) simultaneously; secondary ablations (Table 2 dependency-level D1..Dinf, Table 3 pruning-level P0-P2) hold the max context window fixed while varying representation/pruning depth, giving a budget-matched comparison for those specific tables.

Table 4's RAG ablation (retrieval on vs. off) is run at the same fixed 10,240-token context window on the same >10k-token subset — the retrieval mechanism is the sole varied factor at matched budget; a separate ablation (Tables 2-3) varies fine-tuning context-window size (4,096 vs. 10,240) as its own factor.

Headline comparison (Table 2, RepoScope vs. SimpleRAG/RepoCoder/DRACO/CodeAgent/RLCoder) varies both the context representation/retrieval mechanism and, only approximately, the token budget — not strictly held constant; the internal ablation (Table 3) removing one of the four context views at a time is closer to a budget-matched comparison since it holds the max prompt length (4096) and retrieval pipeline fixed.

Ablations remove one agent/memory component at a time (working memory, multiple patch selection, bug reproduction, regression testing) from the full system while holding model and prompts fixed — varies mechanism/pipeline components, not a token-budget-matched representation comparison.

Central comparison varies the context-management mechanism (fixed-window observation masking vs LLM-generated running summary) at run time; token budget/cost is the measured outcome rather than a held-constant control variable across arms.

Comparison across direct prompting, sliding-window RAG, function-chunking RAG, AST-based retrieval, and agentic exploration varies representation/mechanism and token/context budget simultaneously (agentic methods use ~100x more tokens), so accuracy gains cannot be attributed to representation alone.

Compression method is the sole varied factor: LongCodeZip, LLMLingua variants, RAG, DietCode, SlimCode, and random pruning are compared at matched compression ratios/token budgets against the same uncompressed baseline and target LLM.

The central comparison (raw truncated whole-file concatenation vs. RepoCoder/GraphCoder/RLCoder retrieval-augmented context) holds the 2,048-token budget fixed while varying only the representation/retrieval mechanism used to select cross-file content — a budget-matched representation ablation; however the headline Table 5 numbers combine this with model fine-tuning, so representation and fine-tuning effects are not cleanly separated in the top-line results.

CPCAgent and SPAAgent are added incrementally on top of a base workflow; both context representation and total token/cost budget vary together across the ablation arms, so gains are not isolated to representation choice alone.
Table 1 compares pruning methods at fixed compression-ratio targets (4x/8x) — the pruning method is the sole varied factor at matched output budget across compared baselines and SWE-Pruner.

comparison is 'flat methods' vs. hierarchical TREEFRAG compression — representation and budget change simultaneously (compression is itself the budget reduction), so this is not a budget-held-constant ablation; full methodology and baseline details unverified since full text was unreachable

Table 2's headline comparison (SWE-Adept vs. SWE-agent/RepoGraph/LocAgent/OrcaLoca) varies both representation (dependency tree with lazy skeleton loading) and exploration mechanism (agent-directed DFS vs. free-form or embedding-based baselines) jointly, at unmatched token budgets; later ablations (Tables 4-6) isolate individual components.

central comparison (full-context vs. agent vs. agent+CCE) varies representation, retrieval mechanism, and effective context length/cost together — not a fixed-budget ablation; caller-graph availability, agent tool access, and token consumption all differ simultaneously across arms

Central comparison varies the compression mechanism (learned segment-relevance filtering vs generic token-level LLMLingua-2 vs perplexity-ranked LongCodeZip vs reranker-based SWE-Pruner) at roughly similar target ratios, but actual achieved token budgets differ substantially across methods, so ratio and method quality are confounded.

Compression ratio (budget) is held constant between LaMR and the reproduced SWE-Pruner baseline (Sec 4.1: 'all methods are evaluated under matched compression constraints'); only the pruning representation/mechanism (single CRF vs. dual-rubric CRF + MoE gating) varies.

Main comparison varies the retrieval mechanism (dual-view similarity + RCG-derived usage patterns) and the test-driven iterative planning mechanism simultaneously against baselines lacking both, with prompt token count also differing across arms — representation, retriever, and budget are all confounded.

The central comparison (text-only vs. vision-only vs. multimodal SeeRepo) varies both representation and modality, and token/cost are the measured outcomes rather than held constant, so this is an ablated/measured comparison, not a budget-matched one.

Table 1 compares multiple pruning methods (LLMLingua2, Selective Context, RAG, Self-Prune, LongCodeZip, SWE-Pruner, SWE-Pruner Pro) under identical agent/backbone configuration but without a matched output-token constraint — each method's own quality-vs-token-savings trade-off point is reported rather than budget being equalized across methods.

This is the study's central comparison: representation/mechanism (lexical BM25, structural RepoMap, five embedding models, logged agentic Codex-CLI context) is varied while token budget is explicitly held constant via the BCY@B metric -- the cleanest budget-matched ablation in this batch.

Eager vs Compact holds retrieved candidates identical (same top-10 dense ranking) and isolates the context-retention/delivery policy (frozen injection vs one-time deterministic history rewrite) as a true budget-matched ablation; the further comparison against grep/read varies both retrieval mechanism and token budget together, conflating retrieval quality with delivery policy.

Compares Paritok-4B against GPT-5 and GPT-4.1-mini used as ad hoc compressors on the same trajectories/downstream agent (Claude Sonnet); compression ratios are NOT held constant across the three compressors (25.7% vs 50.2% vs 61.9%), so quality-retention differences are confounded with how aggressively each compressor happens to compress.
